How to Delete KCPtun

A safe, interactive guide to identifying and removing the KCPtun accelerator from your Linux server. Choose your installation method below to generate the correct removal commands.

warning Note: Most commands require root or sudo privileges.

Uninstall via Script

Most automated install scripts (like Teddysun's or ClangCN's) include an uninstall feature. You typically just need to run the script again or run a dedicated uninstall file.

arrow_forward Method A: The "Uninstall" Argument

Many scripts accept an uninstall argument directly.

root@server:~# ./kcptun.sh uninstall

arrow_forward Method B: Re-run the Installer

If you don't see an uninstall file, run the original install script. It often opens a menu.

root@server:~# ./kcptun.sh
# Then look for an option like "4. Uninstall KCPtun"
settings_system_daydream

Manual Removal (Systemd)

If you installed the binary manually and set up a system service, you need to stop the service, disable it, and remove the files.

1

Stop and Disable the Service

Stops the running process and prevents it from starting on boot.

root@server:~# systemctl stop kcptun
root@server:~# systemctl disable kcptun

info If your service is named differently (e.g., kcp-server), replace kcptun with that name.

2

Remove Service File

Deletes the systemd configuration file.

root@server:~# rm /etc/systemd/system/kcptun.service
root@server:~# systemctl daemon-reload
3

Delete Binary & Config

Removes the actual program and its settings. Check typical paths below.

# Common location 1
root@server:~# rm -rf /usr/local/kcptun
# Common location 2
root@server:~# rm -rf /root/kcptun
layers

Docker Removal

If you are running KCPtun inside a container, you simply need to stop the container and remove the image.

search Find Container Name

Run docker ps to see running containers. We assume the name is kcptun below.

# 1. Stop the container
root@server:~# docker stop kcptun
# 2. Remove the container
root@server:~# docker rm kcptun
# 3. Remove the image (optional cleanup)
root@server:~# docker rmi cndocker/kcptun
search

Let's Find KCPtun

Run these commands one by one to see how KCPtun is running on your server.

Test 1: Is it a running process?
ps -ef | grep kcp

If found: It will show a line like /usr/bin/kcptun .... The path shown is where the file is located. You can delete that file and kill the process.

Test 2: Is it a system service?
systemctl list-units --type=service | grep kcp

If found: It will show something like kcptun.service. Go to the "Manual Binary" tab and follow the systemd instructions using that name.

Test 3: Is it in Docker?
docker ps | grep kcp

If found: It will list a container ID and name. Go to the "Docker" tab.
